mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 320d engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a BMW 320d costs £900-£5,800 depending on condition and generation. Used engines start from £900, reconditioned units range from £2,200-£4,800, and fully rebuilt engines with warranty cost £3,200-£5,800. Fitting adds £500-£1,000 depending on the specialist and your location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 320d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include a rattling noise from the engine on cold start that lasts 1-2 seconds, rough idling, and a check engine light. If the chain stretches further, you may experience poor performance, misfires, and eventually catastrophic engine failure if the chain snaps.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 320d?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on the condition of the car. A typical 320d is worth £2,900-£9,700 depending on generation and condition. If your car is in excellent condition with good bodywork and interior, a rebuilt engine at £3,200-£5,800 can be a worthwhile investment. For a sub-£4,000 car, a used engine or targeted repair is usually more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 320d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical engine replacement takes 2-3 days for a specialist, including removal of the old unit, fitting the replacement, and testing. Some suppliers offer next-day delivery on used engines, but fitting always requires workshop time.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the N47 and B47 engines in the 320d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N47 (2007-2014) has a rear-mounted timing chain that is prone to stretching and failure. The B47 (2014-present) relocated the timing chain to the front of the engine, making it more durable and easier to service. The B47 also features improved emissions technology including AdBlue SCR injection to meet Euro 6 standards.

mainEntity.name: Does a rebuilt BMW 320d engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind. Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier before purchase.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 320d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 320d debuted in March 1998 as a milestone in BMW diesel history - the first 3 Series diesel to combine direct injection with an exhaust turbocharger. Over five generations, the 320d badge has become synonymous with diesel efficiency and performance, evolving through three distinct engine families - M47, N47 and B47 - each bringing significant improvements in power, economy and reliability.

milestones.description: M47D20, 1.95L turbo-diesel four-cylinder, 136 hp (E46, distributor-type injection pump)
M47D20TÜ, 2.0L common-rail diesel, 150 hp (E46 facelift, common rail injection)
N47D20, 2.0L common-rail diesel, 163 hp (E90 generation, new engine family)
N47D20A, 2.0L common-rail diesel, 177 hp (E90 LCI, revised variant)
N47D20C, 2.0L common-rail diesel, 184 hp (F30 generation, further revision)
B47D20A, 2.0L common-rail diesel, 163-190 hp (F30 LCI, modular engine family)
B47D20B, 2.0L common-rail diesel, 190 hp (G20 generation, latest variant)

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 320d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 320d has been powered by three generations of four-cylinder diesel engines - the M47, N47 and B47 - each with its own set of well-documented weaknesses. The N47 timing chain crisis has created an entire secondary market for replacement engines, with many owners opting to replace rather than repair due to labour costs exceeding £2,000. Rebuilt units supplied through our network include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 320d N47 Engine Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The N47's rear-mounted timing chain design is prone to stretching and tensioner failure. When the chain stretches, it can skip teeth or snap, causing pistons to hit valves and leading to catastrophic engine failure. Cold-start rattle is the early warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 320d is worth £2,900-£9,700 depending on generation, mileage and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. For vehicles valued under £4,000, a used engine or timing chain replacement is usually the most cost-effective route. For cars worth £4,000-£8,000, a reconditioned unit can be viable if you plan to keep the car for 2+ years. For vehicles worth £8,000+, a rebuilt engine with warranty typically justifies the premium.
problems.recommendation: For N47-engined 320ds, preventative timing chain inspection at 80,000 miles is essential. If you hear cold-start rattle, have the chain inspected immediately - replacement costs £1,200-£2,200 at a specialist, far less than the £3,200-£5,800 for a full engine replacement. For B47-engined cars, timing chain issues are far less common and should not be a primary concern.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N47D20C BMW 3 Series 320d engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 320d B47 Engine Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler develops leaks, allowing coolant to enter the exhaust system. This can lead to white smoke from the exhaust, loss of coolant without visible leaks, and engine overheating. If the EGR cooler fails completely, it can cause significant engine damage due to excessive heat.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler, flush coolant system
repairOptions.longevity: Essential if symptoms present; prevents overheating
When overheating has caused head gasket or block damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 320d of B47-generation (2014-present) is worth £5,000-£25,000 depending on condition and mileage [THIRD-PARTY]. For vehicles under £8,000, an EGR cooler replacement is almost always the better financial decision. Full engine replacement only makes sense if the car is in excellent condition or has high retained value.
problems.recommendation: If you notice white smoke from the exhaust or unexplained coolant loss in your B47-engined 320d, have the EGR cooler inspected immediately. Replacement at a specialist costs £500-£1,000 - a fraction of the cost of a full engine replacement. Regular coolant checks and using BMW-approved coolant can help extend EGR cooler life.
